title: Two State Proposition 47 grants: the treatment beds ran half empty

beats.text: 47 percent.

visual.label: of treatment beds occupied, second grant

beats.text: That’s how full the treatment beds were, in the City’s second Proposition 47 grant.

visual.label: of treatment beds occupied, second grant

beats.text: The target was 90. The first grant managed 66.
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The figures come from the health department’s own evaluations.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: A State board awards Proposition 47 grants for treatment and services.

steps.name: Board of State and Community Corrections

beats.text: San Francisco’s health department won two, 6 million dollars each.

steps.name: Board of State and Community Corrections

beats.text: The evaluations name the Salvation Army’s logs for the residential beds.

visual.label: Salvation Army
visual.sub: residential treatment, named in the evaluations

beats.text: The beds were the core of both grants.

visual.label: Salvation Army
visual.sub: residential treatment, named in the evaluations

beats.text: The first lead is the beds. The first grant ran from 2017 to 2020.

visual.label: Promoting Recovery and Services for the Prevention of Recidivism

beats.text: Occupancy swung from 1 percent to 95 percent, quarter by quarter.
In the second grant, 2019 to 2023, withdrawal and residential beds: 47 percent.
Were empty beds still paid for, as reserved capacity? The reports don’t say.

visual.line: Empty beds may still have been paid for as reserved capacity; the reports do not say.

beats.text: The second lead: the grants’ own promises. 17 objectives in all.
How many were not met, almost met, not reported, or had no data?

visual.label: objectives not met, almost met, not reported or with no data

beats.text: Only 44 percent left residential treatment with a care plan. The target was 100.

visual.title: Other promises
rows: Left residential treatment with a care plan, first grant
Referred to case management, second grant

beats.text: In the second grant, 29 percent of those assessed were referred to case management, against 40.
71 percent of those who saw a case manager got a plan, against 100.
And neither grant measured jail bed days.

visual.sub: jail bed days, in either grant

beats.text: These are self-assessments. The health department commissioned them, as the State requires.

visual.line: The objectives are the grant’s own promises to the State.

beats.text: Missing nearly half, in a self-evaluation, is for the State board to follow up.

visual.line: The objectives are the grant’s own promises to the State.

beats.text: The third lead. One objective, on reoffending, was scored target met.
On how many prior convictions?
Six.

visual.label: convictions on record, up to 6 months prior

beats.text: A measure on a handful of cases can’t show the program lowered reoffending.

visual.line: There were very few convictions on record for PRSPR participants.

beats.text: The evaluator cites COVID-19 closures, slow referrals, a late start and staff turnover.

visual.label: COVID-19 closures
visual.sub: slow referrals, a late start, staff turnover

beats.text: Treatment that depends on court and jail referrals fills slowly when those systems slow down.

visual.label: COVID-19 closures
visual.sub: slow referrals, a late start, staff turnover
